glosses: communication, intercourse (concept of information exchange)

examples.text: Обще́ние в широ́ком смы́сле сло́ва существу́ет не то́лько в че­лове́ческом о́бществе, но и в живо́тном ми́ре, а в на́ши дни мы должны́ та́кже учи́тывать обще́ние челове́ка с маши́ной.
examples.translation: Communication, in the broadest sense of the word, exists not only in human society, but also in the animal kingdom. In our days however, we must also take into account communaction between man and machine.
examples.english: Communication, in the broadest sense of the word, exists not only in human society, but also in the animal kingdom. In our days however, we must also take into account communaction between man and machine.

Гурин видел в нём инженера-руководителя, общение с которым — любая, даже самая мимолётная встреча — обогащает.

glosses: способ взаимодействия с природой, животными и т. п.; пребывание в эмоциональной, духовной, интеллектуальной связи с кем-либо, чем-либо

glosses: The act or fact of communicating anything; transmission.

examples.text: communication of smallpox
communication of a secret

glosses: The concept or state of exchanging data or information between entities.

examples.text: Some say that communication is a necessary prerequisite for sentience; others say that it is a result thereof.
The node had established communication with the network, but had as yet sent no data.

glosses: A message; the essential data transferred in an act of communication.

examples.text: Surveillance was accomplished by means of intercepting the spies' communications.

glosses: The body of all data transferred to one or both parties during an act of communication.

examples.text: The subpoena required that the company document their communication with the plaintiff.

glosses: An instance of information transfer; a conversation or discourse.

examples.text: The professors' communications consisted of lively discussions via email.
Argument […] and friendly communication.

glosses: A passageway or opening between two locations; connection.

examples.text: A round archway at the far end of the hallway provided communication to the main chamber.
The Euxine Sea is conveniently situated for trade, by the communication it has both with Asia and Europe.
This communication between the tank and pump is controlled by a float valve in the tanks and a cock in the pipe, while a poppet valve prevents the undrawn liquor going into the waste tank.

glosses: A connection between two tissues, organs, or cavities.

examples.text: ...and here a free communication had been established between the aorta and the vena cava.

glosses: Association; company.

examples.text: Evil communications corrupt good manners.

glosses: Participation in Holy Communion.

examples.text: We admit them in the Church to a right of Communication to drink of the Cup of the Bloud of Christ.

glosses: A trope by which a speaker assumes that his hearer is a partner in his sentiments, and says \"we\" instead of \"I\" or \"you\".

examples.text: Communication[…]takes place when a speaker or writer assumes his hearer or reader as a partner in his sentiments and discourse, saying We, instead of I or Ye.

examples.text: Yet do I vnderſtand your darkeſt language, / Your treads ath'toe, your ſecret iogges and vvringes: / Your entercourſe of glaunces: euery tittle / Of your cloſe Amorous rites I vnderſtand, / They ſpeake as loud to mee, as if you ſaid, / My deareſt Dariotto, I am thine.
this sweet intercourse of looks and smiles

And indeed, what more reliable authority could Berlioz have found than Cavaillé-Coll, with whom he had frequent intercourse, and who would have been better qualified than any one else to give him correct information?

It was a joy to snatch some brief respite, and find himself in the rectory drawing–room. Listening here was as pleasant as talking; just to watch was pleasant. The young priests who lived here wore cassocks and birettas; their faces were fine and mild, yet really strong, like the rector's face; and in their intercourse with him and his wife they seemed to be brothers.

Texto o documento escrito que informa sobre algo de manera oficial o formal.
Tratado que un profesional o académico presenta en su disciplina o área del saber, especialmente en congresos o reuniones de especialistas en su campo.

Figura retórica por la cual se refuerza el propio punto de vista mediante el diálogo o consulta con un interlocutor, asumiendo o dando por hecho que tiene el mimo parecer o criterio, sin realmente esperar respuesta.

examples.text: L'avantage de fragmenter le bois raméal réside dans l'augmentation des surfaces de contact pour les décomposeurs et l'établissement de conditions abiotiques propices à l'évolution des populations microbiennes, ce qui est de nature à favoriser l'incorporation des composés azotés au sol.
Ces deux corps sont en contact.

glosses: Liaison ; relation ; communication.

examples.text: L’opinion publique italienne ne fut pas informée de ces contacts, mais la presse transalpine publia dans les jours précédant l’entrée en guerre de nombreux articles très francophobes.

examples.text: Mais il n’importe pas seulement de connaître les finesses du métier, il faut surtout être perspicace pour ce qui est répréhensible, nous voulons parler des moyens frauduleux auxquels se livrent peu ou prou tous ceux faisant commerce de chevaux.

examples.text: Ce doit être, interrompis-je, un homme d’un commerce charmant ; la douceur de sa voix, quand il a répondu à l’interrogatoire du commissaire de police, m’a frappé.
